# Synthetic media fixtures

All images are 32 × 20 pixels before orientation. The RGB pattern and RGBA pattern were generated for Recast, without external artwork.

- `rgb.png`: opaque RGB pattern.
- `rgba.png`: RGBA pattern including opaque, partially transparent, and fully transparent colored pixels.
- `photo.jpg`: JPEG encoding of the RGB pattern.
- `rotated.jpg`: the JPEG with one EXIF orientation entry set to 6 (90° clockwise); normalized output is 20 × 32.
- `metadata.png`: RGB pattern with orientation 6 in eXIf and an sRGB profile generated by Little CMS.
- `linear-rgb.png`: RGB pattern with a synthetic linear-gamma RGB profile generated by Little CMS, using sRGB primaries and a D65 white point. Color conversion should change pixel values; retaining versus stripping metadata should not change the final pixels.
- `rgba.webp`: lossless encoding of `rgba.png`, retaining invisible RGB values (`webp:exact=true`).
- `photo.webp`: lossy WebP encoding of `photo.jpg` at quality 80.
- `rotated.webp`: lossless encoding of `metadata.png`, preserving its orientation 6 and ICC profile without rotating its pixels.
- `animated.webp`: a two-frame animation of `rgba.png` and `rgb.png`, with 100 ms frame delays and infinite looping. Used to verify that still-image conversions reject animation.

The WebP fixtures were generated with the pinned ImageMagick 7.1.2-32 worker. Tests also modify RIFF lengths and animation flags to exercise malformed WebP handling.

The BMP fixtures were assembled from their headers and pixel rows in Python, independently of the converter under test. Their RGB pattern uses `R = 8x`, `G = 12y`, and `B = 5(x+y) mod 256`:

- `rgb.bmp`: 24-bit Windows V3, uncompressed, bottom-up rows.
- `top-down.bmp`: the same RGB pixels with negative height and top-down rows.
- `core.bmp`: the same RGB pixels with a 12-byte OS/2 core header.
- `rgba.bmp`: Windows V4 with explicit RGBA bit masks; alpha cycles through 0, 128, and 255 by column. Tagged as sRGB.
- `palette.bmp`: uncompressed 8-bit V3; pixel index is `x + 3y`, palette RGB is `(i, 255-i, 5i mod 256)`.
- `rle.bmp`: the same indexed pixels encoded as RLE8, with explicit row/end markers.
- `rle4.bmp`: RLE4 with a 16-color palette and pixel index `(x + 3y) mod 16`.
- `rgb565.bmp`: 16-bit V3 bitfields with RGB565 masks; channels are `(x, 3y mod 64, (x+y) mod 32)` before expansion.
- `profiled.bmp`: RGB pixels in a V5 BMP with the synthetic linear-gamma ICC profile from `linear-rgb.png` embedded after the pixels.

BMP tests independently inspect exported 24-bit pixel bytes, padding, and header layout. They create odd-width, truncated, malformed-header, embedded-image-wrapper, bitmap-array, and concatenated/forged-size variants in temporary directories.

The TIFF fixtures are assembled independently by `python3 src-tauri/tests/fixtures/generate_tiff.py`, using the same RGB pattern as BMP. The script uses only Python's standard library:

- `rgb-le.tiff`, `rgb-be.tiff`: classic TIFF in both byte orders.
- `bigtiff-le.tiff`, `bigtiff-be.tiff`: the same pixels using BigTIFF directories and 64-bit offsets.
- `rgba.tiff`: straight 8-bit alpha cycling through 0/128/255 by column, including nonzero hidden RGB.
- `associated.tiff`: premultiplied version of that pattern; decoding involves 8-bit rounding.
- `gray16.tiff`: unsigned 16-bit grayscale, `(1901x + 97y) mod 65536`; values intentionally differ from an 8-bit ramp.
- `rgba16.tiff`: unsigned 16-bit RGBA, `(1901x, 3101y, 997(x+y))`, alpha 0/32768/65535; tests inspect actual exported sample bytes, including hidden RGB.
- `planar.tiff`, `tiled.tiff`: separate RGB planes and 16×16 tiles, including partially used edge tiles.
- `deflate.tiff`, `packbits.tiff`: independently encoded lossless compressed strips (Python zlib and literal PackBits runs).
- `palette.tiff`: the indexed pattern and palette used by BMP.
- `rotated.tiff`: orientation 6, description/artist, synthetic XMP and IPTC metadata.
- `profiled.tiff`: the synthetic linear RGB ICC profile from `linear-rgb.png`.
- `multipage.tiff`: two valid image directories sharing the pixel payload.

TIFF tests also create LZW/JPEG/Group4 sources with the bundled worker, verify the actual compression tags, and convert them through Recast. Malformed directory counts, offsets, truncated pixels, corrupt Deflate, unsupported compression/samples, and subimage/layer/raw markers are exercised in temporary files. XMP retention/stripping is checked across PNG/JPEG/WebP/TIFF.

The tests create corrupt and animated-PNG-marker variants in temporary directories. Existing outputs, output naming conflicts, and cancellation files are also isolated to temporary directories.

GIF/animation fixtures are generated by `python3 src-tauri/tests/fixtures/generate_animation.py`. GIF headers, palettes, clear/literal LZW codes, interlacing, controls, looping, and expected canvases are assembled with Python’s standard library. WebP containers are assembled independently around existing still WebP payloads; the synthetic linear ICC profile comes from `linear-rgb.png`.

- `still.gif`, `interlaced.gif`: 32×20 four-color pattern, cut-out transparency; the latter uses an interlaced local palette.
- `disposal.gif`, `forever.gif`, `once.gif`, `max-loops.gif`: 8×6 animation with partial frames, restore-previous/background disposal, zero delay, and 3/infinite/1/65,536 total plays.
- `identical.gif`: three identical frames with independent 20/30/40 ms delays and two total plays.
- `disposal-frames.json`: independently composed RGBA canvases for the disposal fixture.
- `partial.webp`: partial rectangles with blend/replace and background disposal on a transparent 40×24 canvas; the first payload is opaque.
- `millisecond.webp`, `fast.webp`, `long-delay.webp`: exact 33/33/34/0 ms, 1/5/10/20 ms, and maximum 24-bit WebP frame delays.
- `profiled-animation.webp`: linear ICC, orientation 6, and XMP attached to the full animation container. Tests verify color conversion/orientation before retaining or stripping metadata.

Tests construct malformed flags/bounds/lengths, oversized sequences, corrupt LZW, and tampered output timing in temporary directories. Chrome additionally decodes the generated outputs independently for pixel, timing, and looping checks.

Audio fixtures are generated independently with macOS CoreAudio by `python3 src-tauri/tests/fixtures/generate_audio.py`. The checked-in files let every CI platform exercise Apple's encoder output without requiring Apple codecs. They contain synthetic stereo samples at 48 kHz, 5,003 frames, using the low `bits / 8` bytes of `(i * 104729 * 7919) mod 2^32` for each interleaved sample. Rust reconstructs these samples independently and compares decoded PCM bytes.

- `apple-16.m4a`, `apple-24.m4a`: 16/24-bit Apple Lossless, accepted and decoded exactly.
- `apple-32.m4a`: valid 32-bit Apple Lossless, rejected clearly at inspection. The bundled FFmpeg decoder cannot handle all 32-bit ALAC frames; Recast currently accepts only 16/24-bit ALAC.
- `unsupported-aac.m4a`: AAC at 128 kb/s, verifying that an M4A container is not mistaken for ALAC. AAC support is a later increment.

The initial files were generated on macOS 26.5.1. Container metadata may differ when regenerated; the PCM pattern is deterministic. Separate local checks also used CoreAudio to decode Recast's 16/24-bit ALAC output and compare every sample against the same independent pattern.

MP3 input fixtures use the standalone LAME 4.0 executable, independently of Recast's FFmpeg integration: `python3 src-tauri/tests/fixtures/generate_mp3.py /path/to/lame`. The source is synthetic 16-bit stereo PCM, 44.1 kHz, 44,117 frames; left/right tones are 431/997 Hz with amplitudes 9000/7000, truncated to integer samples. The generator disables ReplayGain analysis. CI reads the checked-in files without needing a standalone LAME installation.

- `lame-vbr.mp3`: V2 variable bitrate, ordinary title/artist tags, and a LAME/Xing gapless header.
- `lame-crc.mp3`: 192 kb/s constant bitrate with MPEG CRC protection, exercising raw `FF FA` recognition and gapless decoding.
- `lame-no-xing.mp3`: 128 kb/s without a Xing/LAME header; tests retain its full decoded frames because exact encoder delay/padding is unavailable.

MP3 tests independently reconstruct the original tones and check channel integrity and decoded sample count, rather than requiring lossy samples to equal the source. Tests also encode every supported rate, verify CBR bitrates, short/partial-frame lengths, retained tags, explicit compatibility choices, PCM defaults, clipping/retry, malformed/truncated/concatenated input, and active cancellation. The 12 kHz / 12,117-frame case reproduces FFmpeg 9.0.2's trailing-padding overwrite and verifies the checked muxer correction. Local mpg123 1.33.7 independently decodes VBR/CBR outputs at 12/44.1/48 kHz and verifies exact gapless lengths and the synthetic tone content.
